Inflationary pressures rise globally, impacting food and land prices

Global inflation is showing an upward trend, with specific concerns arising from increased prices of sugar, chips, pork, and eggs in various regions. In Japan, land prices have risen for the fifth consecutive year, and monks are turning to investments due to worsening inflation. The Bank of Japan is reportedly poised to raise its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.25% to combat intensifying inflation risks fueled by rising oil and import costs. Meanwhile, in Jammu and Kashmir, inflation has reached 4.09%. The Reserve Bank of India had previously noted few signs of generalized price pressures but may need to consider rate hikes next month.
